description: After the Mission is an interactive NASA Space Apps 2026 web museum exploring real equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Through six NASA-backed exhibits, an animated Moon, guided tours, artifact comparisons, and learning challenges, visitors discover what these machines did, why they stayed behind, and the science they made possible. NASA imagery and sources bring space history to life for students and curious explorers.
summary: After the Mission is an interactive digital museum bringing NASA’s forgotten spacecraft back to life. Using NASA datasets, mission archives, and authentic imagery, we created an immersive experience exploring abandoned lunar equipment, Mars rovers, and historic missions. Through interactive maps, timelines, scientific discoveries, and engaging storytelling, our project makes space exploration accessible and shows how these machines continue to shape humanity’s understanding of the universe.
details:
After the Mission is an interactive digital museum created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to bring abandoned and retired NASA spacecraft back to life by combining scientific research, interactive technology, and immersive storytelling.

Our website allows visitors to explore historic missions through interactive Moon and Mars maps, spacecraft exhibits, timelines, scientific visualizations, and educational activities. Each exhibit explains a spacecraft's original purpose, technological achievements, discoveries, final moments, and lasting scientific legacy. We also explored integrating an AI-powered museum guide to help visitors navigate the experience and understand complex scientific concepts.

Technology and Development

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code. We incorporated NASA mission archives, scientific resources, and authentic space imagery to create an educational experience grounded in real scientific information.

Despite having limited traditional programming experience, we used AI-assisted development tools, including ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex, to accelerate coding, research, debugging, and prototyping. This allowed us to transform ambitious ideas into interactive features within the hackathon's limited timeframe.

Innovation and Impact

What makes our project unique is its combination of scientific storytelling, cinematic design, and interactive exploration. Rather than simply presenting historical facts, we wanted visitors to experience the stories behind humanity's greatest robotic explorers.

Throughout development, we prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility, intuitive navigation, performance, and educational value.

Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, particularly among students and younger audiences, while demonstrating how modern technology can make scientific knowledge more engaging and accessible.

Ultimately, After the Mission shows that even when a spacecraft's mission ends, its contribution to humanity's understanding of the universe continues.
